topic: Diffusing Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide
scope: NCBI Bookshelf chapter on how to interpret DLCO, including the percent-predicted range, conditions that raise or lower it, and the Va and Kco components.

keyRecommendations.text: A DLCO below the 75% to 140% predicted range indicates reduced capillary blood volume or fibrosis of the alveolar-capillary interface.
Pulmonary hemorrhage is among the conditions that increase DLCO. Anemia, pulmonary vascular disease, and early ILD lower DLCO when lung volumes are normal.
Restriction with a normal DLCO suggests an extrapulmonary cause. DLCO reflects alveolar volume (Va) and the rate of CO uptake (Kco).

clinicalBottomLine: Interpret a low DLCO as a gas-transfer problem, then use volume and the clinical pattern. Hemorrhage can raise DLCO. Anemia and vascular disease can lower it. Restriction with a normal DLCO points outside the lung parenchyma.
notableCaveats: The 2017 ERS/ATS single-breath technical standard is not in PMC. This Bookshelf chapter is the open interpretive text. Spirometry-only and carbon-monoxide poisoning papers were not used.
